paragraphs: This is less a tale of one person than the story of humanity's search, as Swamiji told it. It begins with a small spark of love in human hearts, a love that, he admitted, has not grown very much even now. At first it reached only as far as one's own tribe. Each tribe had its own god, its protector, and members sometimes saw themselves as that god's descendants, the way clans trace themselves back to a founder. Some ancient royal lines even claimed descent from the Sun and the Moon.

As these tribes grew, a little affection and sense of duty to one another appeared, and with it some social order. People realised they could not live together without bearing with each other and holding back their impulses. Restraint, Swamiji said, is the foundation of all society; anyone who never learns to bear and forbear lives a miserable life.

Then religion brought a glimpse of something higher and more ethical, and the old gods began to look out of place: rowdy, quarrelsome, fond of drink and the smoke of sacrifices. People started asking why the gods acted as they did, and no good reasons came. So humanity kept the qualities it could accept, dropped the rest, and combined them into one God of gods: no longer just a symbol of power but a moral being who loved and helped mankind, the most good and most powerful being in the universe.

But this patchwork could not hold. The grander God became, the bigger the puzzle grew. If an all-powerful, all-loving God rules the world, why is there so much suffering and wickedness? We can look away, Swamiji said, but the world remains harsh, like the torment of Tantalus, who could never reach the water and fruit just in front of him.

We are driven by cravings we cannot satisfy and by ideals we cannot express. Give up ideals and we sink to the level of animals; reach for them and we suffer even more. Both roads seem to lead to misery, and no explanation fixes it. Yet Swamiji promised that Vedanta shows the way out. Its truths may sometimes startle you, he said, but if you think them over and absorb them, they will lift you up and help you live in truth.
learn: Our ideas about the highest truth have grown over time, and they can keep growing in each of us. When life feels unfair or frustrating, don't settle for either giving up your ideals or ignoring reality; keep thinking honestly until you find a deeper answer.
